title: Oikos run log entry
description: One line of a run log (JSONL). The kernel is the only writer. Entry hash = SHA-256 over the bytes 'oikos.log.v1\n' followed by the canonical JSON (RFC 8785 / JCS) of the entry without its 'hash' field; 'prev' is the previous entry's hash (64 zeros for the header). Commands are the only replay inputs; events, checkpoints and the end entry are regenerated on replay and must match byte for byte; annotations are carried through verbatim. So replay can regenerate the entire log and compare it byte-identically.

seq.description: 0 for the header, then +1 per entry.

t.description: Kernel sim time when the entry was written.

build.description: Kernel build identity (git commit, '+dirty' if uncommitted). Replay on a different build is reported, not silently accepted.

run_id.description: Minted by the orchestrator; opaque to the kernel.

config_hash.description: SHA-256 of 'oikos.config.v1\n' + canonical JSON of config.

Command.description: An input to the kernel. The orchestrator sends these; the kernel logs each one before applying it. Participant identity is bound by the orchestrator, never taken from a participant's own message.

as.description: The position it acts in (absent: as itself, a person's only). The kernel checks it holds it.

by.description: Who does the act's work, if not the actor alone: people, each alive, present and at work (`orchestration.performers_in`). The act's time is theirs, shared between them; it starts when all are free. Absent: the actor. Foundations step F3.

reasoning.description: The participant's own stated reasoning, if it gave any. Logged, never interpreted.

thinking.description: World seconds spent deciding before the act starts (the world's thinking_time, docs/design/rebuild.md 6.4): the act begins after it. Absent: none.

to.description: Advance the clock to this time, processing every scheduled effect (payments, completions, expiries) with time <= to, in (time, scheduling order).

only.description: Only this capacity ('self', or a position it holds); absent: all of them.

oneOf.description: An observation that also looks through the named channels now (attention).

only.description: Only this capacity ('self', or a position it holds); absent: all of them.

oneOf.description: An entity's record, set (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10d). The platform's bookkeeping for that entity, named in the world's config, never an act in the world: it takes no time. With no `entity`, the participant's own person's record; with one, an organisation whose keeping post (`keeps_record`) the participant now holds. The kernel refuses it (never logged) for an entity with no bookkeeping named for its record (a participant's `record_keeper`, a code controller's module, or the keeping post's role module), so whatever a model decides, it cannot write who it is; and it refuses a record that would hold more than the world's caps.entity_record_bytes: a record never grows. Logged in every log, lean ones too: it is state.

entity.description: The organisation whose record is set, when it is not the participant's own person's: one for which the participant now holds a position whose definition has keeps_record. Absent: the participant's own person's record. Anything else is refused and never logged.

set.description: Sections of the record, by name: each given replaces the section of that name whole; the rest stand. The kernel reads none of them (whole numbers only, as all opaque data). What a person's sections are: entity-record.schema.json.

because.description: What moved it, in the mind's own short terms: a list of happenings (what, about whom, how much). Logged and chained with the change; never read by the kernel.

Provenance.description: How the blocks came to be. Kernel logs it but never uses it to decide anything.

draft_hash.description: Hash of the signed-off draft (see participant-api Draft). The proposer signed exactly this.

Event.description: Every change to the world emits at least one event, each pointing at the command that caused it. There are no events for law: laws are records (the 'recorded' event) and nothing happens because of them unless someone acts.

oneOf.description: An entity's own record was set: its n-th change; `chain`, the hash of this change (t, set, because, in canonical JSON) over the chain before it ('oikos.entity_record.v1\n' + previous chain + change; the first has no previous); `digest`, the hash of the record's sections as they now stand. With these the record can be rebuilt from the log and checked (`oikos record`).

keeper.description: Who keeps this entity's record under the world's config (the name of the bookkeeping module): by whose bookkeeping the change was made. Not part of chain or digest. Absent in logs written before it was named.

RefusalCode.description: Stable reasons the kernel refuses an act. PHYSICS AND MECHANICS ONLY: there is no code for 'illegal', because the kernel doesn't know the law (D19). 'boundary_protected': the outside world's edge account can't be closed. 'not_in_position': the participant doesn't hold the position it acted in. 'not_theirs': the position or system isn't the acting organisation's (only an organisation can fill its own positions). 'participant_inactive': it left the study without a stand-in, or ended. 'not_modelled': the world has no physics for it (no life.birth, no life.harm).

Annotation.description: Information about the run that is not world state: token usage and cost, LLM transcripts, translator drafts and sign-offs, debriefs. Chained like everything else (so tampering is detected), ignored by the state machine, copied verbatim on replay.

cost_microusd.description: Cost of this call in millionths of a US dollar, from the price table recorded in the orchestrator annotation.

annotation.description: transcript: raw exchange with a participant's controller (prompt as rendered, response). translation_failure: proposal the translator could not compile (the failure log that tells us which blocks are missing). debrief: post-run debrief exchange (VISION §15.3). orchestrator: orchestrator version, price tables, participant-controller bindings. observation: an observation a participant received, in full (data: t, as, observation), written only when the run is asked to record that participant's observations (docs/design/run-datasets.md). decision: a code citizen's decision, as its mind made it (data: t, domain, strategy, choice, options with their scores in basis points, and, where the mind decided, each option's facts, others, meaning and learned, with current, circumstances, satisfied_here, doubt and, on a citizen's first, person: the dataset contract's CitizenDecision says each; docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7), written for full logs unless the run was asked not to: training data for citizen models. outcome: what a code citizen came to know, since its last action, of how its choices turned out (data: outcomes, a list; each: t, when the citizen came to know it; domain and option, the area of life and what it is about, as its decisions name them; of, the decision it follows from, by that decision's n, absent where no recorded decision began it; kind, what happened in a word; way, how the citizen came to know: mine, here, published or ask; from, who told it; facts, what happened; learned, the mind's update of what it has learned of the option: payoff, before, after, first, heard; need; felt; belief: the dataset contract's CitizenOutcome says each; docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7). Facts as the citizen had them and the mind's own figures: nothing in it says whether an outcome was good, and nothing the citizen did not know. Written wherever decisions are, and left out with them. decision data carries n, the citizen's own count of its recorded decisions, which an outcome's of names. audit: a truth audit's divergence (data: t, unit, belief, expected, found, since: when it was first found), written in test and calibration runs only, and only for a divergence still there at the unit's next audit (docs/design/rebuild.md 8.2). decision data may carry the mind's state (contracts-0.7 A2). model_call_failed: a model call that failed after its adapter's own time limits and retries, recorded where its transcript would have been (data: purpose, ref if the call had one, t, provider, model, system_sha256, turn, input: as a transcript's; error: the failure, in words; no output, and no usage annotation goes with it). The run went on (the participant waited that wake), so a resumed run is served the failure as a failure at the same point.

state_hash.description: SHA-256 of 'oikos.state.v1\n' + canonical JSON of the full world state (including PRNG state and id counters).

Anchor.description: One line of the witness file (<log>.anchors.jsonl), written outside the log to a location the participants cannot reach. Not part of the chain.

wall_time.description: Informational only; never used by the world.
